abstract: BLS The Economics Daily (Sept 15, 2026): the labor share of output in the US nonfarm business sector was 52.8% in Q2 2026, the lowest level recorded since the series began in 1947. The share was generally 60–66% through much of the postwar period, began a sustained decline after 2000 with large drops following the 2001 and 2007–09 recessions, stabilized after 2010, spiked temporarily to 58.9% in Q2 2020, and then resumed a mostly downward trend. The note makes no claim about AI.
keyFindings: Nonfarm business labor share: 52.8% in Q2 2026, lowest since 1947.
Temporary spike to 58.9% in Q2 2020 before resuming its decline.
methodology: BLS Productivity program estimate: labor compensation (wages, salaries, benefits, pensions, employer social-insurance contributions, other earnings) as a share of nonfarm business sector output; quarterly, 1947Q1–2026Q2.
qualifiers: Tier 1: official BLS statistic. The note attributes nothing to AI; the decline long predates generative AI. Measured labor share is sensitive to depreciation, pass-through relabeling of wages as profits, and timing of stock compensation (see the Goldman decomposition reported by Fortune, fortune-goldman-labor-share-2026), so it is not a direct read on median wages.
